title: Year 12 Investigating Science Module 8 – Science and Society
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Investigating Science Module 8, organised by its three Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How do science-related events affect society’s view of science?

questions.prompt: What medical development led to the eradication of smallpox?
What transport achievement developed from scientific and engineering advances in aerodynamics?
What type of accident can damage public confidence in nuclear power?
What large structure can provide hydroelectricity but also disrupt river ecosystems?
What term describes the overall image or reputation of science held by the public?
Scientific events can affect public trust positively or negatively depending partly on how their risks and benefits are what?
What energy source relies on controlled nuclear reactions and can be affected by public responses to reactor accidents?
What word describes possible harm associated with a scientific technology or event?
What branch of philosophy deals with what is right and wrong in scientific research?
What process requires participants to agree knowingly and voluntarily to take part in research?
What principle protects participants’ private information in research?
What form of research involving human embryos is specifically subject to ethical regulation?
questions.answer: Embryo research. Accept: genetic modification of embryos.

questions.prompt: What type of medical research must be regulated to protect participants when new medicines are tested?
What type of biological weapon research raises major international ethical and security concerns?
What Indigenous rights area protects traditional knowledge, cultural expressions and associated knowledge?
questions.answer: Indigenous cultural and intellectual property. Accept: ICIP.

questions.prompt: What broad purpose of regulation aims to prevent harmful or unacceptable outcomes from scientific research?
questions.answer: Protection. Accept: protecting people, society and the environment.

categories.name: How do economic, social & political forces affect research?

questions.prompt: What resource determines how much money is available for a research project?
What sector may fund research because of potential market opportunities and profit?
What institutions often compete for limited research grants and project budgets?
What political body can influence research priorities through public funding decisions?
What technology uses remotely operated or autonomous aircraft for tasks such as monitoring and research?
What medical strategy has contributed to the eradication or control of infectious diseases worldwide?
What process makes contaminated water safer for human use and improves public health?
What term describes sharing benefits when research or products use Indigenous knowledge or biological resources?

finalRound.prompt: What four broad influences does the syllabus emphasise when evaluating how society affects science and scientific research?
finalRound.answer: Ethical, social, economic and political influences.
